plannerAnswers.question: What did you like most about this prompt?
plannerAnswers.answer: It gives the director freedom to choose a coherent game while making completion concrete: a polished vertical slice, controller-first UX, attract mode, live tuning, multiplayer, and honest feedback. Letting builders choose their own randomized title also preserves their creative ownership.

plannerAnswers.question: What was confusing?
plannerAnswers.answer: The source label combines the regional names Stone Sling and Smithereens! and supplies 1980, while the references found associate Stone Sling with 1981 and the US manual with 1982. Multiplayer also leaves open whether standalone means same-device versus or independent online matchmaking; the Hub client supplies hosted sessions but no standalone room service.

plannerAnswers.question: What was the hardest thing to do?
plannerAnswers.answer: Turning a very simple simultaneous charge-and-release duel into a substantial, authorable demo without losing its identity or inheriting the engine kit's turn-based rules. The plan also had to connect timing-sensitive controls, structural destruction, headless authority, and the Hub lifecycle into one testable design rather than separate feature lists.

plannerAnswers.question: What would you change in this prompt?
plannerAnswers.answer: Identify the source platform and regional title explicitly, distinguish the supplied source year from a verified release date, and state whether standalone multiplayer must support online rooms or whether local versus plus Hub online play satisfies it. Define a short hosted-match format separately from the longer solo demo, and use explicit output-name placeholders when a plan will be shared across builders.
